long.description:
In February 1959, nine experienced hikers died on the slopes of Kholat Syakhl — the "Dead Mountain" — in Russia's Ural Mountains. Their tent was slashed open FROM THE INSIDE. They fled barefoot into minus-thirty cold. Their bodies showed injuries like a car crash, yet their skin was unmarked. Their clothing was radioactive. And one victim's tongue was missing.

What really happened on the Dead Mountain that night? An avalanche? Secret military tests? Or something no science has named?
